correctness.rationale: The residual-polynomial identity yields the approximate-inverse polynomial acting on the right-hand side. Exact reduction shows degree one is a positive scalar and degree two is a positive multiple of the matrix formed by subtracting the Stieltjes matrix from a larger diagonal matrix, hence entrywise nonnegative. In dimension two, exact endpoint eigenvalues force an affine functional calculus whose off-diagonal coefficient has the required sign and whose diagonal entries are positive. The rational three-dimensional witness has the stated three eigenvalues; exact arithmetic gives the negative third coordinate and a strictly positive exact solution. The checker replays the finite rational algebra, while the universal statements are proved symbolically.

value.rationale: Chebyshev semi-iteration is a standard acceleration method valued for spectral minimax convergence without inner products. On inverse-positive Stieltjes systems, coordinatewise nonnegativity is a separate structural property. Locating the first possible loss simultaneously in iteration degree and matrix dimension gives a sharp boundary rather than an isolated example: degree two is universally safe, dimension two remains safe at degree three, and a three-dimensional exact witness fails.
